---
title: "Data Quality and Provenance"

---

Imagine that you are a city official charged with determining whether schools in your district meet lead (Pb) exposure standards. Sampling in the district is done by various testing companies, using various instruments, each with a given nominal precision. State and city procedures mandate that each measurement be replicated at least once (preferably more). The instruments have known biases that can be corrected for.

Lead concentrations can be reported in several units:

| Unit name | Abbreviation | Equivalent to 400 ppm (EPA play area limit) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Parts per million** | ppm | 400 ppm |
| **Milligrams per kilogram** | mg/kg | 400 mg/kg |
| **Micrograms per gram** | µg/g | 400 µg/g |
| **Parts per billion** | ppb | 400,000 ppb |
| **Percent by weight** | % | 0.04% |

The recommended thresholds also vary by medium:

| Medium | Specific target type | EPA threshold value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Paint / Dust** | Liquid/surface paint limit | 90 ppm (0.009%) |
| **Soil** | Bare soil, child play areas | 400 ppm |
| **Tap water** | Public utility action level | 10 ppb (0.010 mg/L) |

## 1. Where did this value come from?

### 1.1 A spreadsheet from a new employee

One day, a new employee of yours hands you a spreadsheet that looks like this:

::: {.pond-dq-notes}
| Sample ID | Location | Value | Safe? |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | :---: |
| PB-001 | FAIRVIEW ELEM. | 12 | Yes |
| PB-002 | LINCOLN MIDDLE | 150 | Yes |
| PB-003 | ROOSEVELT HIGH | 0.03 | Yes |
| PB-004 | JEFFERSON ELEM. | 420 | No |
| PB-005 | WASHINGTON ELEM. | 8 | Yes |
:::

[Fictional schools and values created for The Pond (2026).]{.pond-dq-credit}

**Your turn!**

Four of the five schools are marked safe. Before you report that to the city council:

1. How do you think the **Safe?** column was decided?
2. What would you need to know to check it yourself?

```{=html}
<div class="pond-dq">
  <label for="pond-dq-new-employee"><strong>My observations</strong></label>
  <textarea id="pond-dq-new-employee" class="pond-dq-response" rows="4"
    placeholder="Write your answers here..."></textarea>
</div>
```

<details class="pond-dq-reveal">
<summary>Compare with our answer</summary>

Each value must be an average of replicates, but the spreadsheet doesn't say **of how many samples**, **in what units**, or **with what precision**. Nor does it say what was sampled, so you can't tell which threshold applies.

A **Safe?** column is not a reproducible determination: without the information behind it, you can't check it.

</details>

### 1.2 The same spreadsheet, from a senior employee

Now suppose that the exact same spreadsheet had come from your most senior employee, who has done this work for twenty years.

**Your turn!** Would you trust it more?

```{=html}
<div class="pond-dq-whatif" role="group" aria-label="Would you trust it more?">
  <button type="button" class="pond-dq-tag" aria-pressed="false" data-verdict="It's natural to give an experienced colleague more credit. But look again: the table is identical, so it contains no more evidence than before.">Yes, more</button>
  <button type="button" class="pond-dq-tag" aria-pressed="false" data-verdict="Right: the table is identical, so it contains no more evidence than before.">No, the same</button>
</div>
<p class="pond-dq-take" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
```

<details class="pond-dq-reveal">
<summary>Why it matters</summary>

The employee's experience is not the relevant variable here; **metadata** are. An experienced person may have years of precedent to justify how they do things, but also more unstated assumptions. If you are not operating with the same assumptions, their spreadsheet may lead you astray. We will come back to trust and reputation in Activity 5.

</details>

### 1.3 A better dataset

Here is the same survey, with the information that was missing:

::: {.pond-dq-notes .pond-dq-wide}
| Sample ID | Location | Medium | # replicates | Instrument | Value | Units | Precision | Threshold | Safe? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | ---: | :--- | ---: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| PB-001 | FAIRVIEW ELEM. | Tap water | 3 | Lab spectrometer | 12 | ppb | ± 1 | 10 ppb | No |
| PB-002 | LINCOLN MIDDLE | Soil | 2 | Handheld analyzer B | 150 | ppm | ± 15 | 400 ppm | Yes |
| PB-003 | ROOSEVELT HIGH | Paint | 2 | Handheld analyzer A | 0.03 | % | ± 0.005 | 0.009% | No |
| PB-004 | JEFFERSON ELEM. | Soil | 4 | Handheld analyzer B | 420 | ppm | ± 20 | 400 ppm | No |
| PB-005 | WASHINGTON ELEM. | Tap water | 1 | Lab spectrometer | 8 | ppb | ± 1 | 10 ppb | Yes |
:::

Two schools have changed from "Yes" to "No." The new employee had applied the soil threshold, 400, to every row, whatever the medium and units.

**Your turn!**

1. Which stage of the data has actually been archived?
2. Can the processed value be traced back to the original observations?
3. What transformations occurred?
4. Are those transformations documented?
5. Could another researcher reproduce the processed value?

```{=html}
<div class="pond-dq">
  <label for="pond-dq-better-dataset"><strong>My observations</strong></label>
  <textarea id="pond-dq-better-dataset" class="pond-dq-response" rows="5"
    placeholder="Write your answers here..."></textarea>
</div>
```

<details class="pond-dq-reveal">
<summary>Compare with our answer</summary>

1. **The average.** Each value summarizes several replicate measurements.
2. **No.** The individual replicates have not been archived, and they should be.
3. **Averaging, then comparison with a threshold.** (The bias corrections mentioned at the start may have been applied too; the table doesn't say.)
4. **Not explicitly.** They can be inferred from the metadata: the reported medium tells us which units and threshold were likely used. It would be better to make this explicit.
5. **Not without the actual workflow:** which replicates went into each average, which corrections were applied, and how. See [What is a Workflow?](../../workflow/what-is-a-workflow/index.qmd)

Did you spot that WASHINGTON ELEM. has only **one** replicate? The procedures require at least two measurements, so that "Yes" should not stand until the school is resampled.

</details>

### 1.4 How could we do better?

Even the better table can't answer every question. Some of the evidence you need lives **outside** the numerical dataset.

**Your turn!** Which of these would you ask the testing companies for? Select as many as you like, then reveal what each one would tell you.

```{=html}
<div id="pond-dq-evidence" class="pond-dq"></div>
```

<!-- Ancillary evidence. data-name is the label on the button; the text inside is revealed. -->

::: {#pond-dq-evidence-bank}
::: {.pond-dq-evidence data-name="Calibration records"}
Show how each instrument's readings were converted and corrected for its known bias, and when it was last checked.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-evidence data-name="Instrument logs"}
Record errors, maintenance, and failed readings: was the analyzer working properly on the day PB-004 was measured?
:::

::: {.pond-dq-evidence data-name="Field notes"}
Describe the conditions: was the tap at FAIRVIEW ELEM. flushed before sampling? Was the soil at JEFFERSON ELEM. wet?
:::

::: {.pond-dq-evidence data-name="Replicate measurements"}
Let you see how much the replicates disagree, and recompute each average yourself.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-evidence data-name="Standards / reference materials"}
Samples with a certified lead content, measured alongside the real ones, show whether the instrument read accurately that day.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-evidence data-name="Processing code"}
Documents exactly how replicates were averaged, corrections applied, and thresholds chosen, so anyone can rerun or check it.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-evidence data-name="Photographs or images"}
Show where each sample was taken: a play area, or a flower bed by the parking lot?
:::

::: {.pond-dq-evidence data-name="Sample metadata"}
Who collected each sample, when, and how it was stored and handled before analysis.
:::
:::

### Key takeaway

Evidence supporting data quality may exist outside the numerical dataset itself. More metadata tends to be a good thing, but it often involves a tradeoff because it takes time and effort to maintain complete metadata records, so scientists often land on a compromise between what is ideal and what simply "clears the bar" (which is context-dependent, and might evolve over time). 

## 2. What does this number actually mean?

In Activity 1, JEFFERSON ELEM. was reported at 420 ppm of lead in soil, just above the 400 ppm threshold. Before the city closes a playground, it's worth asking what that number really tells us.

### 2.1 Precise, accurate, or both?

To check their instruments, four testing companies each measured the same **reference soil** five times. A reference soil is a sample whose lead content has been certified by a standards laboratory, here at exactly 400 ppm.

**Your turn!** For each analyzer, decide whether its readings are **precise** and whether they are **accurate**.

```{=html}
<div id="pond-dq-analyzers" class="pond-dq pond-dq-cards"></div>
```

<!-- Readings of a reference soil certified at 400 ppm. data-precise and data-accurate (yes/no) are the answers;
     the text inside is revealed once the learner has answered both questions. -->

::: {#pond-dq-analyzer-bank}
::: {.pond-dq-analyzer data-name="Analyzer A" data-readings="360,445,392,418,385" data-precise="no" data-accurate="yes"}
**Accurate on average, but not precise.** The readings average exactly 400, but any single one can be off by 40 ppm or more.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-analyzer data-name="Analyzer B" data-readings="380,500,470,395,455" data-precise="no" data-accurate="no"}
**Neither.** The readings are scattered *and* their average (440 ppm) is too high.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-analyzer data-name="Analyzer C" data-readings="398,401,399,402,400" data-precise="yes" data-accurate="yes"}
**Precise and accurate.** The readings agree with each other *and* with the certified value.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-analyzer data-name="Analyzer D" data-readings="431,433,430,432,434" data-precise="yes" data-accurate="no"}
**Precise, but not accurate.** The readings agree closely, but all of them are about 32 ppm too high. This is a **bias**, like the known biases mentioned at the start. Because it is consistent, it can be measured and corrected.
:::
:::

These four analyzers illustrate three ideas that are easy to confuse:

- **Precision:** how finely or consistently something can be measured. Precise readings agree with each other.
- **Accuracy:** how close a measurement is to the true value. Accurate readings agree with the truth.
- **Uncertainty:** the range of plausible values, and the sources of doubt, associated with a measurement or its interpretation.

Analyzer D shows why the difference matters: precision alone can't tell you whether a measurement is right.

### 2.2 How many digits?

The testing company's spreadsheet reports the average for JEFFERSON ELEM. as:

::: {.pond-dq-notes}
**420.250000 ppm**
:::

The analyzer's nominal precision is **± 20 ppm** per reading.

**Your turn!** How would you report this value to the city council?

```{=html}
<div class="pond-dq-whatif" role="group" aria-label="How would you report this value?">
  <button type="button" class="pond-dq-tag" aria-pressed="false" data-verdict="Too many digits. The last six digits were produced by the spreadsheet, not by the analyzer.">420.250000 ppm</button>
  <button type="button" class="pond-dq-tag" aria-pressed="false" data-verdict="Still too many. With ± 20 ppm, even the ones digit is uncertain; the hundredths are meaningless.">420.25 ppm</button>
  <button type="button" class="pond-dq-tag" aria-pressed="false" data-verdict="Better: no digits beyond what the analyzer supports. But nothing tells the reader how uncertain the value is.">420 ppm</button>
  <button type="button" class="pond-dq-tag" aria-pressed="false" data-verdict="Best: the digits match the precision, and the uncertainty is stated.">420 ± 20 ppm</button>
</div>
<p class="pond-dq-take" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
```

<details class="pond-dq-reveal">
<summary>Why it matters</summary>

Six decimal places don't add information; they add **false precision**. A council member reading "420.250000 ppm" could reasonably assume the lead content is known to a millionth of a ppm, and that it is certainly above 400. Neither is true.

The number of digits reported should reflect the precision of the measurement, not the number of digits produced by software or a spreadsheet.

</details>

### 2.3 How precise is the average?

The 420 ppm for JEFFERSON ELEM. is the average of four replicate readings:

::: {.pond-dq-notes}
| Reading | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | **Mean** | **Standard deviation** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Lead (ppm) | 392 | 447 | 403 | 439 | **420** | **27** |
:::

The readings themselves vary, so the average is uncertain too. If the readings are **independent** (each one a separate, fresh measurement), the uncertainty of the mean is the **standard error of the mean**:

$$\text{SEM} = \frac{\text{standard deviation}}{\sqrt{\text{number of readings}}}$$

For JEFFERSON ELEM., that is 27 / √4 = **13.5 ppm**.

A common rule of thumb is that the true value most likely lies within **2 SEM** of the mean (about 95% of the time).

**Your turn!** Is 420 − 2 × 13.5 above the 400 ppm threshold? In other words, can we be confident that JEFFERSON ELEM.'s soil is above the threshold?

```{=html}
<div class="pond-dq-whatif" role="group" aria-label="Can we be confident that JEFFERSON ELEM. is above 400 ppm?">
  <button type="button" class="pond-dq-tag" aria-pressed="false" data-verdict="Not quite: 420 − 2 × 13.5 = 393 ppm, which is below 400. The plausible range, 393 to 447 ppm, straddles the threshold.">Yes</button>
  <button type="button" class="pond-dq-tag" aria-pressed="false" data-verdict="Right: 420 − 2 × 13.5 = 393 ppm, which is below 400. The plausible range, 393 to 447 ppm, straddles the threshold, so four readings aren't enough to decide.">No</button>
</div>
<p class="pond-dq-take" aria-live="polite" hidden></p>
```

**How many readings would it take?** Move the slider to see how the uncertainty shrinks as you add readings (assuming the mean and standard deviation stay the same).

```{=html}
<div class="pond-dq pond-dq-sem">
  <label for="pond-dq-n"><strong>Number of readings: <output id="pond-dq-n-out">4</output></strong></label>
  <input id="pond-dq-n" type="range" min="1" max="20" value="4" class="form-range">
  <svg id="pond-dq-sem-plot" viewBox="0 0 600 90" role="img" aria-labelledby="pond-dq-sem-text"></svg>
  <p id="pond-dq-sem-text" class="pond-dq-status" aria-live="polite"></p>
</div>
```

<details class="pond-dq-reveal">
<summary>Two important caveats</summary>

**Independence.** The SEM formula assumes each reading is a fresh, independent measurement. Four readings taken without moving the analyzer, or from the same handful of soil, are not independent: they will agree more closely than separate samples would, and the SEM will make you overconfident.

**Bias.** More readings shrink the *random* scatter, but not a bias. Averaging a thousand readings from Analyzer D would give 432 ppm with a tiny SEM: very precise, and still wrong. Only calibration against a reference soil reveals that.

And with WASHINGTON ELEM.'s single reading, you can't compute a standard deviation at all, so there is no way to tell how uncertain it is. That is one reason why procedures require replicates.

(Statisticians would note that with only a few readings, the plausible range is even wider than 2 SEM. We keep things simple here.)

</details>

### 2.4 More than the instrument

The analyzer's ± 20 ppm is only one source of uncertainty. Uncertainty can arise at every stage between the soil in the playground and the number in the spreadsheet.

**Your turn!** Which of these could affect the 420 ppm reported for JEFFERSON ELEM.? Select all that apply, then reveal our take.

```{=html}
<div id="pond-dq-sources" class="pond-dq"></div>
```

<!-- Sources of uncertainty. data-name is the label on the button; the text inside is revealed. -->

::: {#pond-dq-sources-bank}
::: {.pond-dq-source data-name="Instrument precision"}
Each reading is only good to ± 20 ppm.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-source data-name="Calibration"}
If the correction for the analyzer's known bias is off, every reading shifts together, and the replicates won't reveal it.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-source data-name="Replicate variability"}
The readings vary by 27 ppm, more than the analyzer's ± 20 ppm. The soil itself is uneven.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-source data-name="Sample preparation"}
Wet or unsieved soil reads differently from dry, sieved soil.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-source data-name="Processing choices"}
Which readings were kept, how the bias was corrected, and how the average was taken all change the final number.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-source data-name="Units and reporting"}
A value in % read as ppm (remember ROOSEVELT HIGH?) is off by a factor of 10,000.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-source data-name="Spatial sampling"}
Four readings from one spot may not represent a whole playground. More on this in Activity 3.
:::

::: {.pond-dq-source data-name="Temporal sampling"}
Lead in soil can change after renovation work, new mulch, or heavy rain. More on this in Activity 3 too.
:::
:::

### Key takeaway

A reported number is only as meaningful as what we know about its precision, accuracy, and uncertainty. Report only the digits the measurement supports, state the uncertainty, and remember that the instrument is rarely the only source of doubt.

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  // Learner answers stay in this browser only
  const storageKey = "pond-data-quality";
  let saved = { notes: {}, picks: [] };
  try {
    saved = Object.assign(saved, JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(storageKey)) || {});
  } catch (e) {}
  if (!Array.isArray(saved.picks)) saved.picks = [];
  function save() {
    try { localStorage.setItem(storageKey, JSON.stringify(saved)); } catch (e) {}
  }

  // Free-text answers
  document.querySelectorAll(".pond-dq-response").forEach(box => {
    box.value = saved.notes[box.id] || "";
    box.addEventListener("input", () => { saved.notes[box.id] = box.value; save(); });
  });

  // Single-choice buttons that show a short verdict
  document.querySelectorAll(".pond-dq-whatif").forEach(group => {
    const out = group.nextElementSibling;
    group.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(btn => {
      btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
        group.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(b === btn)));
        out.textContent = btn.dataset.verdict;
        out.hidden = false;
      });
    });
  });

  // Part 4: pick the evidence you would request, then reveal what each tells you
  const bank = document.getElementById("pond-dq-evidence-bank");
  const box = document.getElementById("pond-dq-evidence");
  const items = [...bank.querySelectorAll(".pond-dq-evidence")].map(div => ({
    name: div.dataset.name, html: div.innerHTML
  }));
  bank.hidden = true;

  box.innerHTML = `
    <div class="pond-dq-choices" role="group" aria-label="Evidence to request"></div>
    <p class="pond-dq-status" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-primary">Reveal what each one tells you</button>
    <div class="pond-dq-cards" hidden></div>`;
  const choices = box.querySelector(".pond-dq-choices");
  const status = box.querySelector(".pond-dq-status");
  const cards = box.querySelector(".pond-dq-cards");
  const revealBtn = box.querySelector(".btn-primary");

  function updateStatus() {
    const n = saved.picks.length;
    status.textContent = n ? `${n} of ${items.length} selected.` : "Nothing selected yet.";
  }

  items.forEach(item => {
    const btn = document.createElement("button");
    btn.type = "button";
    btn.className = "pond-dq-tag";
    btn.textContent = item.name;
    btn.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(saved.picks.includes(item.name)));
    btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
      const on = btn.getAttribute("aria-pressed") !== "true";
      btn.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(on));
      saved.picks = on ? [...saved.picks, item.name] : saved.picks.filter(p => p !== item.name);
      save();
      updateStatus();
      const card = cards.querySelector(`[data-name="${CSS.escape(item.name)}"]`);
      if (card) card.classList.toggle("is-picked", on);
    });
    choices.append(btn);
  });
  updateStatus();

  revealBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    cards.innerHTML = "";
    items.forEach(item => {
      const card = document.createElement("div");
      card.className = "pond-dq-card";
      card.dataset.name = item.name;
      card.classList.toggle("is-picked", saved.picks.includes(item.name));
      card.innerHTML = `<h4></h4><div class="pond-dq-card-text"></div>`;
      card.querySelector("h4").textContent = item.name;
      card.querySelector(".pond-dq-card-text").innerHTML = item.html;
      cards.append(card);
    });
    cards.hidden = false;
    revealBtn.hidden = true;
  });
  // ---------- Activity 2 ----------

  // 2.1 Precise / accurate cards with a strip plot of readings
  const analyzerBank = document.getElementById("pond-dq-analyzer-bank");
  const analyzerBox = document.getElementById("pond-dq-analyzers");
  saved.analyzers = saved.analyzers || {};
  const lo = 340, hi = 520, x = v => 20 + (v - lo) / (hi - lo) * 260;
  analyzerBank.querySelectorAll(".pond-dq-analyzer").forEach(div => {
    const name = div.dataset.name;
    const readings = div.dataset.readings.split(",").map(Number);
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.className = "pond-dq-card";
    const dots = readings.map(v =>
      `<circle cx="${x(v)}" cy="30" r="6" class="pond-dq-dot"></circle>`).join("");
    card.innerHTML = `
      <h4></h4>
      <svg viewBox="0 0 300 62" role="img" aria-label="${name} readings: ${readings.join(", ")} ppm">
        <line x1="20" x2="280" y1="30" y2="30" class="pond-dq-axis"></line>
        <line x1="${x(400)}" x2="${x(400)}" y1="10" y2="46" class="pond-dq-target"></line>
        ${dots}
        <text x="${x(400)}" y="58" text-anchor="middle" class="pond-dq-label">400 (certified)</text>
        <text x="20" y="58" class="pond-dq-label">${lo}</text>
        <text x="280" y="58" text-anchor="end" class="pond-dq-label">${hi} ppm</text>
      </svg>
      <p class="pond-dq-readings"></p>
      <div class="pond-dq-q"><span>Precise?</span><div class="pond-dq-choices" role="group" data-key="precise"></div></div>
      <div class="pond-dq-q"><span>Accurate?</span><div class="pond-dq-choices" role="group" data-key="accurate"></div></div>
      <div class="pond-dq-take" aria-live="polite" hidden></div>`;
    card.querySelector("h4").textContent = name;
    card.querySelector(".pond-dq-readings").textContent = `Readings: ${readings.join(", ")} ppm`;
    const take = card.querySelector(".pond-dq-take");
    const mine = saved.analyzers[name] = saved.analyzers[name] || {};

    function update() {
      if (!mine.precise || !mine.accurate) return;
      const right = mine.precise === div.dataset.precise && mine.accurate === div.dataset.accurate;
      take.innerHTML = `<p>${right ? "✓ You got it." : "Not quite."}</p>` + div.innerHTML;
      take.hidden = false;
    }

    card.querySelectorAll(".pond-dq-choices").forEach(group => {
      const key = group.dataset.key;
      group.setAttribute("aria-label", `${name}: ${key}?`);
      ["yes", "no"].forEach(value => {
        const btn = document.createElement("button");
        btn.type = "button";
        btn.className = "pond-dq-tag";
        btn.textContent = value === "yes" ? "Yes" : "No";
        btn.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(mine[key] === value));
        btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
          mine[key] = value;
          save();
          group.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(b === btn)));
          update();
        });
        group.append(btn);
      });
    });
    update();
    analyzerBox.append(card);
  });
  analyzerBank.hidden = true;

  // 2.3 Slider: mean ± 2 SEM against the 400 ppm threshold
  const nSlider = document.getElementById("pond-dq-n");
  const nOut = document.getElementById("pond-dq-n-out");
  const semPlot = document.getElementById("pond-dq-sem-plot");
  const semText = document.getElementById("pond-dq-sem-text");
  const mean = 420, sd = 27, px = v => 30 + (v - 340) / (500 - 340) * 540;
  function drawSem() {
    const n = Number(nSlider.value);
    nOut.textContent = n;
    if (n < 2) {
      semPlot.innerHTML = `<text x="300" y="45" text-anchor="middle" class="pond-dq-label">One reading: no standard deviation, so no way to estimate the uncertainty.</text>`;
      semText.textContent = "With a single reading, the uncertainty of the mean can't be estimated.";
      return;
    }
    const half = 2 * sd / Math.sqrt(n);
    const a = mean - half, b = mean + half;
    const above = a > 400;
    semPlot.innerHTML = `
      <line x1="30" x2="570" y1="40" y2="40" class="pond-dq-axis"></line>
      <line x1="${px(400)}" x2="${px(400)}" y1="12" y2="62" class="pond-dq-target"></line>
      <text x="${px(400)}" y="80" text-anchor="middle" class="pond-dq-label">400 ppm threshold</text>
      <rect x="${px(a)}" y="32" width="${px(b) - px(a)}" height="16" rx="8" class="pond-dq-range ${above ? "is-above" : ""}"></rect>
      <circle cx="${px(mean)}" cy="40" r="6" class="pond-dq-dot"></circle>
      <text x="30" y="80" class="pond-dq-label">340</text>
      <text x="570" y="80" text-anchor="end" class="pond-dq-label">500 ppm</text>`;
    semText.textContent = `${n} readings: 420 ± ${half.toFixed(0)} ppm (${a.toFixed(0)} to ${b.toFixed(0)} ppm). ` +
      (above ? "The whole range is above 400 ppm." : "The range still includes values below 400 ppm.");
  }
  nSlider.addEventListener("input", drawSem);
  drawSem();

  // 2.4 Pick the sources of uncertainty, then reveal
  saved.sources = Array.isArray(saved.sources) ? saved.sources : [];
  const sourceBank = document.getElementById("pond-dq-sources-bank");
  const sourceBox = document.getElementById("pond-dq-sources");
  const sources = [...sourceBank.querySelectorAll(".pond-dq-source")].map(div => ({
    name: div.dataset.name, html: div.innerHTML
  }));
  sourceBank.hidden = true;
  sourceBox.innerHTML = `
    <div class="pond-dq-choices" role="group" aria-label="Sources of uncertainty"></div>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-primary">Reveal our take</button>
    <div class="pond-dq-take" hidden></div>
    <div class="pond-dq-cards" hidden></div>`;
  const sourceChoices = sourceBox.querySelector(".pond-dq-choices");
  const sourceCards = sourceBox.querySelector(".pond-dq-cards");
  const sourceTake = sourceBox.querySelector(".pond-dq-take");
  sources.forEach(s => {
    const btn = document.createElement("button");
    btn.type = "button";
    btn.className = "pond-dq-tag";
    btn.textContent = s.name;
    btn.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(saved.sources.includes(s.name)));
    btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
      const on = btn.getAttribute("aria-pressed") !== "true";
      btn.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(on));
      saved.sources = on ? [...saved.sources, s.name] : saved.sources.filter(p => p !== s.name);
      save();
    });
    sourceChoices.append(btn);
  });
  sourceBox.querySelector(".btn-primary").addEventListener("click", e => {
    const n = saved.sources.length;
    sourceTake.innerHTML = `<p><strong>All ${sources.length} of them.</strong> You selected ${n}. ` +
      `Uncertainty is not just instrument error: it can enter at every stage between the soil and the spreadsheet.</p>`;
    sourceCards.innerHTML = "";
    sources.forEach(s => {
      const card = document.createElement("div");
      card.className = "pond-dq-card";
      card.classList.toggle("is-picked", saved.sources.includes(s.name));
      card.innerHTML = `<h4></h4><div class="pond-dq-card-text"></div>`;
      card.querySelector("h4").textContent = s.name;
      card.querySelector(".pond-dq-card-text").innerHTML = s.html;
      sourceCards.append(card);
    });
    sourceTake.hidden = false;
    sourceCards.hidden = false;
    e.target.hidden = true;
  });
});
</script>
